changes: Re-segmented 'dvijavara śrīsaśidevātmaja pravoddanārtha': read as 'dvijavara-śrī-Śaśideva[na] ātmaja-prabodhanārtha[ṃ]' ('by the excellent brahmin Śaśideva, to instruct his son'). The instrumental 'vāsina' (= vāsinā) needs an agent noun, and a scribe naming himself only as 'son of X' would be unusual. Śaśideva is therefore the scribe and owner (svaṃ pustakaṃ), not merely the father.
Removed p1 'Śaśidevātmaja' as a person. The son is not named, so he appears only in purpose and notes. The son_of relation is removed as well.
Date: 'aśukla' read as Āśvina śukla. On śukla 5 the Moon in Jyeṣṭhā puts the Sun around Kanyā, which fits amānta Āśvina. Set month Āśvina and pakṣa śukla. NS 586 ≈ 1466 CE is kept.
Purpose rewritten as instruction of the scribe's son; the book is his own.
Place as_written is now the full phrase; Patan is kept (Lalitabruma/Lalitapura, Mānīgala).

notes: 'śrīsaśidevātmaja pravoddanārtha' is ambiguous. The preferred reading is Śaśideva as scribe and owner, writing to instruct his unnamed son (ātmaja-prabodhanārtham), with 'vāsina' as an instrumental agent. The alternative is that the scribe is an unnamed son of Śaśideva copying for his own study. 'aśukla' is most likely Āśvina śukla: Jyeṣṭhā on śukla 5 implies the Sun is in Kanyā. The cataloguer marked the year 586 with (!), so it may be misread. NS 586 = 1466 CE, but the weekday has not been verified. 'Laḍitabrumā' = Lalitabruma/Lalitapura (Patan); 'Mānīgala' = Maṇigal, the palace area. 'pitho' may be a corruption of 'pīṭha' or of a locality name.
